title: Clean and normalise the Silver claims
prompt:
Silver holds the claims the business can trust. Two problems remain in the rows that passed: the export repeats some claims exactly, and when a payer asks for changes the clinic resubmits the visit's claim under a new `claim_id`, later. Only the latest submission counts.

Write `silver_claims(claims, providers)`: the rows of `checked_claims` with no reason, each claim once, one claim per visit, in Silver's tidy columns.
rules: Start from the rows of `checked_claims(claims, providers)` with no `_reason`. Exact copies (every column the same) count once.
Keep one claim per `encounter_id`: the one submitted last. If two share that `submitted_date`, keep the larger `claim_id`.
`submissions` is how many different claims the visit had after copies were removed (1 when it was never resubmitted).
`days_to_submit` is the days from `service_date` to `submitted_date`. A missing `paid_amount` becomes 0.00: nothing paid yet.
hints: `dropDuplicates()` with no columns removes exact copies only. Do it before counting submissions.
`Window.partitionBy("encounter_id").orderBy(F.col("submitted_date").desc(), F.col("claim_id").desc())` with `F.row_number()` puts the latest submission first; keep row 1.

`F.count("*").over(Window.partitionBy("encounter_id"))` counts each visit's claims on every row. `F.datediff(end, start)` counts days, and `F.coalesce("paid_amount", F.lit(0).cast("decimal(12,2)"))` keeps the column's type.
explanation: Two kinds of repeats need two tools. An exact copy is the same row twice, so `dropDuplicates()` on every column removes it without choosing anything. A resubmission is a different claim for the same visit, so a key-based rule decides: rank each visit's claims by `submitted_date`, newest first, with `claim_id` as a tie-breaker so the choice is the same on every run, and keep the first. Removing copies first matters: otherwise a copied claim would look like two submissions. The window count records how many claims a visit had, so nothing about the resubmission is lost. Silver also settles meanings once for every reader: days to submit are computed here, and a missing paid amount is written as 0.00 so the Gold sums never mix in NULLs. The provenance columns travel with every row.
